name: W25X40CLSNIG
title: 4 Mbit serial flash memory with 4 KB sectors and dual I/O SPI, 2.3 V to 3.6 V
summary: The W25X40CL is a 4 Mbit (512 Kbyte) serial flash memory on SPI, with standard single-bit transfers plus dual-output and dual-I/O reads, running from one 2.3 V to 3.6 V supply. Pages of 256 bytes program in about 0.4 ms; erase goes by 4 KB sector, 32 KB or 64 KB block, or whole chip. The clock reaches 104 MHz (208 Mbit/s on two lines) from 2.7 V, and 80 MHz from 2.3 V. Protection comes from status register bits over the top or bottom of the array, the /WP pin and a power-down state; each part carries a 64-bit unique ID.

pins.name: /CS
pins.function: Chip select, active low. High deselects the part and floats DO (IO0, IO1); a falling edge begins each instruction and a rising edge ends it. After power-up it has to go from high to low before the first instruction is taken.

pins.name: DO (IO1)
pins.function: Serial data output in standard SPI, shifted on the falling edge of CLK; becomes bidirectional IO1 under the dual instructions.

pins.name: /WP
pins.function: Write protect, active low. With the SRP bit at 1, holding it low blocks writes to the status register, and so locks the TB and BP2-BP0 protection setting.

pins.name: DI (IO0)
pins.function: Serial data input for instruction, address and data bits, latched on the rising edge of CLK; becomes bidirectional IO0 under the dual instructions.

pins.name: CLK
pins.function: Serial clock. Inputs are taken on its rising edge; outputs change on its falling edge.

pins.name: /HOLD
pins.function: Hold, active low. Taken low while /CS is low, it pauses the part: DO goes high impedance and DI and CLK are not looked at. Taking it high again carries on from where it stopped.

operation.text: 512 Kbyte (524,288 bytes) in 2048 pages of 256 bytes. A program writes from 1 to 256 bytes of one page. Erase works on 128 sectors of 4 KB, 16 blocks of 32 KB, 8 blocks of 64 KB, or the whole array. The 64 KB blocks run 0 (000000h-00FFFFh) to 7 (070000h-07FFFFh).

SPI modes 0 and 3 are both accepted. They differ only in where CLK idles while /CS rises and falls: low in mode 0, high in mode 3. Bits go in on the rising CLK edge and come out on the falling edge, most significant bit first.

The two dual reads, 3Bh (dual output) and BBh (dual I/O), turn DI and DO into IO0 and IO1 and move two bits per clock, so 104 MHz gives 208 Mbit/s. 3Bh takes its address one bit per clock and outputs two; BBh takes the address two bits per clock as well. IO0 must be released to high impedance before the falling edge of the first output clock.

With /CS low, /HOLD pauses a transfer so the bus can serve another device, keeping the instruction state and any partly loaded page buffer. Hold starts at the falling edge of /HOLD if CLK is low, otherwise at the next falling CLK edge; it ends the same way on the rising edge of /HOLD. During hold DO floats and DI and CLK are ignored. /CS stays low through the whole hold, or the internal logic resets.

Every instruction starts on a falling /CS edge with a one-byte code on DI and ends on the rising /CS edge. A read can be ended after any bit. A write, program or erase must end on a byte boundary, /CS rising only once a whole number of bytes has been clocked in, or it is dropped. While a program, erase or status write runs, only Read Status Register is accepted.

Below VWI the part holds itself in reset and accepts nothing. Once VCC passes VWI, Write Enable, program, erase and Write Status Register stay locked out for tPUW; reads are allowed tVSL after VCC reaches its minimum. /CS has to follow VCC up and down during the ramps; a pull-up on /CS can do it. The part always comes up with WEL = 0, in standby (ICC1), not power-down.

Write Enable (06h) sets WEL; it is needed before every Page Program, sector, block or chip erase and Write Status Register. WEL clears itself when any of those finishes, and Write Disable (04h) clears it directly. Write Disable also cancels a pending 50h.

BUSY (S0) is 1 while a program, erase or status write runs and returns to 0 when it ends; Read Status Register (05h) works throughout and repeats the byte until /CS rises. WEL (S1) shows the write enable latch. BP2-BP0 (S4-S2) and TB (S5) choose the protected range, counted from the top of the array with TB = 0 or the bottom with TB = 1; all ship at 0, nothing protected. S6 is reserved and reads 0. SRP (S7) works with /WP: at 0 /WP does nothing; at 1 the register cannot be written while /WP is low.

01h followed by one data byte, after Write Enable. Only SRP, TB and BP2-BP0 (bits 7, 5, 4, 3, 2) change. The cycle is self-timed and lasts tW, BUSY reading 1; WEL clears at the end. Sent after 50h instead of 06h, the same byte goes to volatile copies of the bits: they take effect within tSHSL2, BUSY stays 0, and the non-volatile bits are not worn.

Code, then a 24-bit address, then data streams out from that address and keeps going, the address counting up, until /CS rises; one instruction can read the whole array. Clock up to fR. Ignored while BUSY = 1.
As Read Data with eight dummy clocks after the address, which lets the clock run up to FR.

In Fast Read Dual I/O the byte M7-M0 follows the address. M5-M4 = 10 makes the next BBh read, after /CS goes high and low again, skip the code byte, starting straight with the address. Any other value returns to normal instructions. M7-M6 and M3-M0 may be 0 or 1. FFFFh, sixteen clocks on IO0, clears the mode. The part has no reset pin: if the host resets while the mode is set, standard instructions go unrecognised until FFFFh is sent.

After Write Enable: code, 24-bit address, then 1 to 256 data bytes into erased (FFh) locations, /CS low throughout and rising on a byte boundary. Past the last byte of a page the address wraps back to its first byte, so a whole page is written from a low address byte of 0, and anything beyond 256 bytes replaces bytes already sent. Self-timed for tPP; refused if that page is protected.

After Write Enable: Sector Erase 20h (4 KB, tSE), Block Erase 52h (32 KB, tBE1) and D8h (64 KB, tBE2) each take a 24-bit address; Chip Erase C7h or 60h takes none (tCE). The erased state is all 1s (FFh). A range holding any protected area is not erased; chip erase is refused if any block is protected.

B9h drops supply current from ICC1 to ICC2 within tDP of /CS rising. In power-down only ABh is recognised, Read Status Register included among those ignored, which also guards against stray writes. ABh alone returns the part to standby within tRES1, /CS held high for that time; ABh followed by three dummy bytes also reads the device ID (12h), with tRES2 to recover. ABh is ignored while BUSY = 1.

90h with address 000000h returns EFh then 12h, alternating until /CS rises; address 000001h returns the device ID first. 92h does the same over two lines, M7-M0 set to FXh. 9Fh returns EFh, memory type 30h and capacity 13h. 4Bh with four dummy bytes returns a 64-bit number set at the factory and unique to each part.
